\chapter{Complexity — NAESAT To Coloring}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.Complexity.NPReductions.NAESATToColoring
\section{Overview}

This module formalises the polynomial-time reduction from
\emph{Not-All-Equal 3-SAT} (NAE-SAT) to \emph{3-Coloring}.
Given a NAE-SAT instance over Boolean variables $x_1,\dots,x_n$ and clauses
$C_1,\dots,C_m$, it constructs an explicit simple graph whose 3-colorability
is equivalent to the satisfiability of the instance,
and proves both completeness and soundness of that correspondence.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[NAE clause satisfaction]
\lean{NAEtoColor.SatisfiesClause}
\label{NAEtoColor.SatisfiesClause}
\leanok
Given a Boolean assignment $\mathit{assign} : V \to \mathtt{Bool}$ and a
Not-All-Equal clause $c$ with three variables $c.v_0, c.v_1, c.v_2$,
$\texttt{NAEtoColor.SatisfiesClause}$ returns $\mathtt{true}$ if and only if
the three assigned values are \emph{not} all equal, i.e.\ at least two of
$\mathit{assign}(c.v_0)$, $\mathit{assign}(c.v_1)$, $\mathit{assign}(c.v_2)$
differ.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[NAE-SAT instance]
\lean{NAEtoColor.NAESat3}
\label{NAEtoColor.NAESat3}
\leanok
A NAE-SAT instance over variable type $V$ is defined as a list of NAE clauses,
i.e.\ $\texttt{NAEtoColor.NAESat3}\;V = \mathtt{List}\;(\mathtt{NAEclause}\;V)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Global NAE-SAT satisfaction]
\lean{NAEtoColor.SatisfiesNAE3}
\label{NAEtoColor.SatisfiesNAE3}
\leanok
\uses{NAEtoColor.NAESat3, NAEtoColor.SatisfiesClause}
Given an assignment $\mathit{assign} : V \to \mathtt{Bool}$ and a NAE-SAT
instance $f$, $\texttt{NAEtoColor.SatisfiesNAE3}$ returns $\mathtt{true}$ if
and only if every clause in $f$ is satisfied by $\mathit{assign}$
(i.e.\ $\texttt{NAEtoColor.SatisfiesClause}$ holds for each clause).
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[NAE-SAT satisfiability]
\lean{NAEtoColor.IsSatisfiable}
\label{NAEtoColor.IsSatisfiable}
\leanok
\uses{NAEtoColor.NAESat3, NAEtoColor.SatisfiesNAE3}
A NAE-SAT instance $f$ over variable type $V$ is \emph{satisfiable} if there
exists a Boolean assignment $\mathit{assign} : V \to \mathtt{Bool}$ such that
$\texttt{NAEtoColor.SatisfiesNAE3}\;\mathit{assign}\;f = \mathtt{true}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Example NAE-SAT instance]
\lean{NAEtoColor.NAE_SAT_Example.nae_sat_eg}
\label{NAEtoColor.NAE_SAT_Example.nae_sat_eg}
\leanok
\uses{NAEtoColor.NAESat3}
A concrete NAE-SAT instance over $\mathrm{Fin}\,5$ consisting of three clauses:
$\langle 0,1,2\rangle$, $\langle 0,1,3\rangle$, $\langle 0,2,4\rangle$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Example assignment]
\lean{NAEtoColor.NAE_SAT_Example.assign_eg}
\label{NAEtoColor.NAE_SAT_Example.assign_eg}
\leanok
A concrete Boolean assignment for $\mathrm{Fin}\,5$ given by
$\![{\mathtt{true}},{\mathtt{true}},{\mathtt{false}},{\mathtt{false}},{\mathtt{false}}]$,
which witnesses satisfiability of \texttt{NAEtoColor.NAE\_SAT\_Example.nae\_sat\_eg}.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[3-colorability]
\lean{NAEtoColor.Is3Colorable}
\label{NAEtoColor.Is3Colorable}
\leanok
A simple graph $G$ on vertex type $V'$ is \emph{3-colorable} if there exists
a proper coloring $G.\mathtt{Coloring}\;(\mathrm{Fin}\,3)$, i.e.\ a map
from vertices to $\{0,1,2\}$ such that no two adjacent vertices share the same
color.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Reduction vertex type]
\lean{NAEtoColor.OutputVertex}
\label{NAEtoColor.OutputVertex}
\leanok
The vertex set of the reduction graph is an inductive type with three
constructors:
\begin{itemize}
  \item $\mathtt{groundNode}$ --- a single ground vertex (colored ``neutral'');
  \item $\mathtt{varNode}\;v$ --- one vertex per variable $v \in V$;
  \item $\mathtt{clauseNode}\;c\;k$ --- three internal gadget vertices
        ($k \in \mathrm{Fin}\,3$) for each clause $c$.
\end{itemize}
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Reduction edge relation]
\lean{NAEtoColor.EdgeRelation}
\label{NAEtoColor.EdgeRelation}
\leanok
\uses{NAEtoColor.NAESat3, NAEtoColor.OutputVertex}
Given a NAE-SAT instance $\mathit{clauses}$, the directed edge relation on
$\texttt{NAEtoColor.OutputVertex}\;V$ is defined by:
(1) $\mathtt{groundNode}$ is adjacent to every $\mathtt{varNode}$;
(2) $\mathtt{varNode}\;v$ is adjacent to $\mathtt{clauseNode}\;c\;i$ when $v$
is the $i$-th variable of clause $c$;
(3) two clause-gadget nodes $\mathtt{clauseNode}\;c\;i$ and
$\mathtt{clauseNode}\;c\;j$ are adjacent when $c \in \mathit{clauses}$ and
$i \neq j$ (forming a triangle within each clause gadget).
All other pairs are non-adjacent.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Reduction graph]
\lean{NAEtoColor.ReductionGraph}
\label{NAEtoColor.ReductionGraph}
\leanok
\uses{NAEtoColor.EdgeRelation, NAEtoColor.NAESat3, NAEtoColor.OutputVertex}
Given a NAE-SAT instance $f$, $\texttt{NAEtoColor.ReductionGraph}\;f$ is the
simple graph on $\texttt{NAEtoColor.OutputVertex}\;V$ whose adjacency is the
symmetrization of $\texttt{NAEtoColor.EdgeRelation}\;f$ restricted to distinct
pairs (no self-loops).
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Clause-gadget node coloring]
\lean{NAEtoColor.clauseNodeColor}
\label{NAEtoColor.clauseNodeColor}
\leanok
Given three Boolean values $a, b, c$ (the truth values of a clause's three
literals) and an index $k \in \mathrm{Fin}\,3$, returns the color in
$\mathrm{Fin}\,3$ assigned to the $k$-th internal clause-gadget node.
The coloring is chosen so that all three gadget nodes receive distinct colors
whenever $(a, b, c)$ is a NAE-satisfying assignment; if the assignment is
not NAE-satisfying, all gadget nodes are colored $0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[NAE-to-coloring coloring map]
\lean{NAEtoColor.naeColoring}
\label{NAEtoColor.naeColoring}
\leanok
\uses{NAEtoColor.OutputVertex, NAEtoColor.clauseNodeColor}
Given a Boolean assignment $\mathit{assign} : V \to \mathtt{Bool}$, defines a
coloring of all vertices of the reduction graph by:
$\mathtt{groundNode} \mapsto 0$;
$\mathtt{varNode}\;v \mapsto 1$ if $\mathit{assign}(v) = \mathtt{true}$, else $2$;
$\mathtt{clauseNode}\;c\;k \mapsto
\texttt{NAEtoColor.clauseNodeColor}\;(\mathit{assign}(c.v_0))\;(\mathit{assign}(c.v_1))\;(\mathit{assign}(c.v_2))\;k$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Completeness of the NAE-SAT to 3-coloring reduction]
\lean{NAEtoColor.NAEtoColorCompleteness}
\label{NAEtoColor.NAEtoColorCompleteness}
\leanok
\uses{NAEtoColor.EdgeRelation, NAEtoColor.Is3Colorable, NAEtoColor.IsSatisfiable, NAEtoColor.NAESat3, NAEtoColor.OutputVertex, NAEtoColor.ReductionGraph, NAEtoColor.SatisfiesClause, NAEtoColor.clauseNodeColor, NAEtoColor.naeColoring}
\difficulty{5}
Let $f$ be a NAE-SAT instance over a variable type $V$, that is, a list of not-all-equal
clauses each naming three variables. If $f$ is satisfiable — some Boolean assignment $V
\to \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ makes the three variables of every clause not all
receive the same value — then the reduction graph of $f$ is 3-colorable, meaning it
admits a proper coloring with the three colors $\{0, 1, 2\}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Soundness of the NAE-SAT to 3-coloring reduction]
\lean{NAEtoColor.NAEtoColorSoundness}
\label{NAEtoColor.NAEtoColorSoundness}
\leanok
\uses{NAEtoColor.EdgeRelation, NAEtoColor.Is3Colorable, NAEtoColor.IsSatisfiable, NAEtoColor.NAESat3, NAEtoColor.OutputVertex, NAEtoColor.ReductionGraph, NAEtoColor.SatisfiesClause, NAEtoColor.SatisfiesNAE3}
\difficulty{6}
Let $f$ be a NAE-SAT instance over a variable type $V$, that is, a list of Not-All-Equal
clauses, each clause naming three variables. Form the reduction graph associated to $f$:
its vertices are a single ground vertex, one vertex for each variable in $V$, and, for
every clause, three gadget vertices; its edges join the ground vertex to each variable
vertex, join each variable vertex $v$ to a clause-gadget vertex whenever $v$ occurs in
the corresponding position of that clause, and, for every clause of $f$, join its three
gadget vertices pairwise into a triangle. If this graph is 3-colorable — that is, its
vertices admit a coloring by $\{0,1,2\}$ in which adjacent vertices receive distinct
colors — then $f$ is satisfiable: there exists a Boolean assignment $\mathit{assign} : V
\to \{\mathrm{true},\mathrm{false}\}$ under which every clause of $f$ has its three
assigned values not all equal.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Correctness of the NAE-SAT to 3-coloring reduction]
\lean{NAEtoColor.NAEtoColorReduction}
\label{NAEtoColor.NAEtoColorReduction}
\leanok
\uses{NAEtoColor.Is3Colorable, NAEtoColor.IsSatisfiable, NAEtoColor.NAESat3, NAEtoColor.NAEtoColorCompleteness, NAEtoColor.NAEtoColorSoundness, NAEtoColor.ReductionGraph}
\difficulty{1}
Let $f$ be a NAE-SAT instance over a variable type $V$, and let $\Gamma(f)$ denote its
reduction graph, the simple graph built from $f$ as described above (a ground vertex
joined to every variable vertex, each variable vertex joined to the clause-gadget
vertices for the clauses in which it occurs, and the three gadget vertices of each
clause joined pairwise into a triangle). Then $f$ is satisfiable if and only if
$\Gamma(f)$ is 3-colorable.
\end{theorem}

\section{Additional declarations}

\begin{definition}[Not-All-Equal clause]
\lean{NAEtoColor.NAEclause}
\label{NAEtoColor.NAEclause}
\leanok
A \emph{Not-All-Equal clause} over a variable type $V$ is an ordered triple
$(v_0, v_1, v_2)$ of variables from $V$. It records the three variables of one
NAE constraint; such a clause is meant to be satisfied by a Boolean assignment
exactly when the values assigned to $v_0$, $v_1$, $v_2$ are not all equal.
\end{definition}
